scholarships.title: Doctoral Scholarship from the University of Innsbruck

existing.description: The University of Innsbruck awards a doctoral scholarship as start-up, interim, bridge or final financing for doctoral candidates, with a monthly allowance of EUR 1,120 for a maximum of 24 months. Funding is granted in six-month blocks confirmed by an interim progress report from the dissertation supervisor, and the 24-month period can be interrupted twice, each interruption not exceeding six months. Applicants must be enrolled as regular students and registered for continuation with a registered dissertation, and must evidence excellent academic success - an excellent grade point average plus normal duration of study - or scientific achievements; a maximum of two resubmissions is possible. The University states that at least 50 per cent of available funding is to be awarded to women in order to promote young female scientists, and that applicants of equal scientific quality are prioritised if they work in the University's main research areas or on project proposals. Payments are made exclusively by SEPA transfer.
eligibility: Enrolled as a regular student at the University of Innsbruck and registered for continuation
Dissertation registration must exist - otherwise the system will not allow an application
Evidence of excellent academic success (excellent GPA plus normal duration of study) or scientific achievements
Exceeding the minimum duration of study must be justified in the curriculum vitae
Members of doctoral colleges are eligible

Priority is given to applicants involved in the University of Innsbruck's main research areas (research areas, research platform and centers, doctoral colleges) and/or applicants co-working on project proposals, if they are of equal scientific quality
Formal compliance does not imply a legal entitlement to funding
existing.eligibility_summary: Doctoral students enrolled as regular students at the University of Innsbruck and registered for continuation, whose dissertation is registered, who can evidence excellent academic success - an excellent grade point average plus normal duration of study (minimum duration plus two tolerance semesters per study/section, with any excess justified in the CV) - or scientific achievements. Members of doctoral colleges are also eligible.
benefits: Up to 24 months of funding, awarded six months at a time
Six-monthly interim review confirmed by the dissertation supervisor
Up to two interruptions of the funding period, each no longer than 6 months
Target of at least 50 per cent of the available funding awarded to women

scholarships.title: ISTA PhD Program (fully funded PhD employment)
scholarships.official_source: Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA)

existing.funding_period: per month (gross, paid 14 times a year)
existing.description: ISTA states that PhD students are employed by the Institute and that all of them receive internationally competitive salaries and full social security coverage, with additional financial support to attend scientific conferences and workshops. ISTA charges no tuition fees and no application fee for its PhD, internship and scholarship programmes. Published gross salaries for 2026 range from EUR 3,053 to EUR 3,673 per month depending on whether the student holds a Bachelor's or Master's degree at admission, are paid 14 times a year, and rise once the Qualifying Exam is passed. All students receive five-year employment contracts and typically complete the programme in 4.5 to 6 years. For the 2027 intake the call opens in late October 2026 with an application deadline of 8 January 2027.
eligibility: Bachelor's or Master's degree at the time of admission - salary level depends on which degree is held
Available to join a research group after three rotations in three different research groups
Must work towards the PhD full-time
Must pass the Qualifying Exam to move from coursework/rotations to thesis research
Admission through the annual ISTA PhD Call
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants to the ISTA PhD Program must hold a Bachelor's or Master's degree, depending on the track, and are recruited into an interdisciplinary programme with three lab rotations in the first year, a qualifying exam in the second year and thesis research thereafter. All PhD students work full-time and are employed by ISTA.
benefits: Employment by ISTA with a 5-year contract
Gross salary of EUR 3,053-3,673 per month in 2026, paid 14 times a year (12 monthly payments plus double payments in June and November)
Salary raise on passing the Qualifying Exam, about 1.5 years into the degree
Full social security coverage including health insurance
Financial support for attending scientific conferences and workshops
No tuition fees and no application fee
Support from the ISTA Grant Office on external funding applications
